reason: Researched this week (WebSearch/WebFetch plus Yahoo daily closes). Sandisk's Oct 29 print was a clean beat-and-raise: FQ1 revenue ~$11.0B vs ~$10.7B est, FQ2 guide $12.2-12.6B and non-GAAP EPS $55-57 pre-split (above ~$53.60 consensus), ~50% of FY27 and two-thirds of FY28 bits under long-term agreements. So the event risk I cut SNDK to 12% for is gone and the thesis is intact. But the stock fell 13.5% on Oct 30, about 6 points worse than a SOX that itself fell 7.1%. Management guided only 'modest' FQ3 pricing, and most of the end-of-decade pipeline is still unsigned. The tape reason for holding 43% cash got stronger, not weaker: Amazon's miss revived AI-capex fears, Intel fell ~28-30%, SOX had its second 6%+ drop in just over a week, CXMT's ~$20B nine-month profit funds new DRAM supply against Micron, and December hike odds are ~75-85% after a Fed hold with two hike dissents. MU (-2.1% on leg) and SNDK (-8.3%) both sit well inside their 16%/20% stops (~$759 and ~$1,004). Re-entering at the Nov 2 close would only reset those stops without changing the bet, so holding beats adding into a broken chip tape or capitulating on a print that confirmed the thesis. OPERATIONAL FLAG FOR NEXT POLL: Sandisk's 8-for-1 split has a Nov 9 record date, and Nov 20 is the first split-adjusted trading day. My SNDK stop is set against an unadjusted $1,255.58 fill, and if the engine does not split-adjust, the ~87.5% optical drop would trigger it. The SNDK leg must be re-entered or exited at the Nov 7 or Nov 14 poll unless the desk confirms split handling.
